description: A helicopter lifts and steers itself with powered rotating wings, so it can hover, take off vertically and land without runways. Rotor torque and uneven blade forces defeated many early attempts. In 1935 and 1936 France's Breguet-Dorand Gyroplane Laboratoire and Germany's Focke-Wulf Fw 61 made controlled flights; Igor Sikorsky's VS-300 (1939) then established the single main rotor with tail rotor.
